correctness.rationale: For each source facet, the affine area multiplier is |det A||A^{-T}x_j|. Equal transformed areas therefore force the quadratic form Q=A^{-1}A^{-T} to take one constant value c on every design node. When t>=4, design exactness applied to the degree-four nonnegative polynomial (u^TQu-c)^2 makes its spherical integral zero, hence Q=cI and A is a similarity. The converse is immediate. The explicit six-node sharpness set is antipodal with an orthonormal positive half, hence is a spherical 3-design, and its displayed nonsimilarity has constant Q-value one on all six nodes.

value.rationale: The source explicitly highlights the tension between spherical-design isotropy and affine covariance: nonconformal maps usually destroy equal facet weights, but it does not say when exceptions are impossible. The finding gives a complete and sharp answer at the first moment order capable of detecting anisotropic quadratic forms. The t=3 counterexample demonstrates a genuine boundary phenomenon rather than a routine restatement, and the theorem cleanly links fourth-order design strength to affine rigidity of the associated equal-area polytope.
